facts.text: Zr was added to as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at nominal x = 0.01, 0.05, and 0.1, with x = 0 serving as the control.
The alloy buttons were melted under Ar and remelted at least five times.
Room-temperature compression used 3 mm × 6 mm cylinders, a strain rate of 1 × 10^-3 s^-1, and a terminal strain of 0.3.
Nanoindentation creep tests used a 10 mN peak load, a 100 s hold, and loading rates of 0.1, 1, and 5 mN/s.
Electrochemical corrosion testing followed 30 min immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl, with polarization from -0.8 to 1.5 V at 1 mV/s.
At x ≥ 0.05, Ni- and Zr-rich Ni7Zr2 precipitates formed at phase boundaries and bridged the FCC and B2 regions.
The Zr-rich phase changed from a discontinuous network at x = 0.05 to a coarse continuous network at x = 0.1.
At moderate Zr content, lattice distortion and fine Ni7Zr2-related precipitates impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding.
At x = 0.1, the more continuous Zr-rich structure promoted a stable protective passive layer that hindered chloride ingress.
Mechanical performance was optimal at x = 0.05, while increasing Zr to x = 0.1 partially reversed the strengthening benefit.
The x = 0.05 alloy reached a yield strength of 1048.7 ± 23.84 MPa, about 48.7% above the Zr-free control.
Corrosion resistance ranked x = 0.1 > x = 0.01 > x = 0.05 > x = 0, making x = 0.1 the best-performing composition in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
